AFG: Home to the oldest oil paintings in the world, discovered in the Bamiyan caves, dating back to 650 AD.
ALB: Albania has over 173,000 bunkers built during communist rule — roughly one for every 14 people. Most are now abandoned or repurposed.
DZA: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area, covering about 2.38 million sq km — nearly the size of Western Europe combined.
AND: Andorra has no airport, no army, and no national currency of its own — it uses the euro despite not being an EU member state.
AGO: Angola is home to the Okavango River, which flows inland into the Kalahari Desert instead of reaching the sea, creating a vast inland delta.
ATG: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches — one for every day of the year — a claim celebrated in local tradition and promoted by tourism boards.
ARG: Argentina is home to the southernmost city in the world: Ushuaia, known as "The End of the World," at the tip of Patagonia.
ARM: Armenia became the first country in the world to adopt Christianity as its official state religion, in 301 AD.
AUS: Australia is the only continent governed as a single nation and is wider than the Moon's diameter (5,000 km vs 3,474 km).
AUT: Austria is the birthplace of composers Mozart, Haydn, Schubert, and Bruckner — more classical composers per capita than any other nation.
AZE: Azerbaijan has more mud volcanoes than any other country — around 400, about a third of all mud volcanoes on Earth.
BHS: The Bahamas sits on one of the world's largest underwater cave systems, the Lucayan Cavern, stretching over 36 km.
BHR: Bahrain is home to the Tree of Life — a 400-year-old mesquite tree growing alone in the desert with no known water source nearby.
BGD: Bangladesh is home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
BRB: Barbados is the birthplace of rum. The oldest known written reference to rum in the world, from 1650, was found on this island.
BLR: Belarus is one of the last countries in Europe to retain the KGB as its official state security service name.
BEL: Belgium produces over 220,000 tonnes of chocolate per year and has more chocolate shops per square kilometre than any other country.
BLZ: Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language and is home to the second-largest barrier reef.
BEN: Benin is considered the birthplace of Vodun (Voodoo), which is officially recognised as a national religion in the country.
BTN: Bhutan is the world's only carbon-negative country — it absorbs more CO₂ than it produces and measures progress by Gross National Happiness.
BOL: Bolivia has two capital cities: Sucre (constitutional) and La Paz (seat of government), and is home to the world's largest salt flat, Salar de Uyuni.
BIH: Bosnia and Herzegovina is home to the Stari Most bridge in Mostar, originally built in 1566 and one of the most celebrated Ottoman bridges in Europe.
BWA: Botswana went from one of the world's poorest countries at independence in 1966 to an upper-middle-income nation within two generations.
BRA: Brazil contains about 60% of the Amazon rainforest, the largest tropical rainforest on Earth, home to 10% of all species on the planet.
BRN: Brunei's Sultan lives in the world's largest residential palace — the Istana Nurul Iman, with 1,788 rooms and 257 bathrooms.
BGR: Bulgaria is the oldest country in Europe to have kept its original name since its founding in 681 AD.
BFA: Burkina Faso means "Land of Incorruptible People" in both Mossi and Dioula, the two main local languages.
BDI: Burundi is one of the world's few landlocked countries with a shoreline on Lake Tanganyika, the world's longest and second-deepest freshwater lake.
CPV: Cabo Verde (Cape Verde) is an archipelago of 10 volcanic islands in the Atlantic, about 570 km off the west coast of Africa.
KHM: Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world, covering 162.6 hectares and built in the 12th century.
CMR: Cameroon is called "Africa in miniature" because it contains nearly every major climate and ecosystem found across the continent.
CAN: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world — over 202,080 km, including the mainland and offshore islands.
CAF: The Central African Republic is home to Dzanga-Sangha, one of Africa's last great rainforests and a haven for forest elephants and western lowland gorillas.
TCD: Lake Chad has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s due to climate change and water demand — making it one of the world's fastest-shrinking lakes.
CHL: Chile is the longest country in the world from north to south — stretching 4,300 km while averaging only 177 km wide.
CHN: China is home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, with over 45,000 km of track — more than the rest of the world combined.
COL: Colombia is the only country in South America with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
COM: Comoros is the world's largest producer of ylang-ylang, a flower used in perfumes including Chanel No. 5.
COD: The DRC contains the Congo River, the world's deepest river at over 220 metres, and the only river that crosses the equator twice.
COG: The Republic of Congo sits directly across the Congo River from the DRC — making Brazzaville and Kinshasa the world's closest capital cities.
CRI: Costa Rica abolished its military in 1948 and has maintained peace ever since, redirecting defence funds to education and healthcare.
CIV: Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast) is the world's largest producer and exporter of cocoa beans, supplying about 40% of the global supply.
HRV: Croatia has over 1,200 islands along its Adriatic coast, making it one of the most island-rich coastlines in the Mediterranean region.
CUB: Cuba has one of the highest literacy rates in the world at over 99%, achieved through a mass literacy campaign launched in 1961.
CYP: Cyprus has the world's only divided capital — Nicosia has been split between the Greek Cypriot south and the Turkish Cypriot north since 1974.
CZE: The Czech Republic consumes more beer per capita than any other country in the world — about 188 litres per person per year.
DNK: Denmark consistently ranks as one of the happiest countries in the world and was the first country to legalise same-sex unions, in 1989.
DJI: Djibouti is home to Lake Assal, the lowest point in Africa at 155 metres below sea level and one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.
DMA: Dominica is known as "The Nature Isle of the Caribbean" and has the second-largest boiling lake in the world, a volcanic feature in its interior.
DOM: The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti — the only island in the Caribbean shared by two sovereign nations.
ECU: Ecuador is home to the Galápagos Islands, whose unique wildlife directly inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection.
EGY: Egypt is home to the only surviving ancient wonder of the world — the Great Pyramid of Giza, built around 2560 BC.
SLV: El Salvador is the smallest and most densely populated country in Central America, and the only one without a Caribbean coastline.
GNQ: Equatorial Guinea is the only Spanish-speaking country in Africa and one of Africa's top oil producers per capita.
ERI: Eritrea is one of the world's newest countries, gaining independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after a 30-year independence struggle.
EST: Estonia is one of the world's most digitally advanced nations — it offers e-residency to non-citizens and conducts elections online.
SWZ: Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is one of Africa's last absolute monarchies and officially renamed itself in 2018 to shed its colonial-era name.
ETH: Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months and is currently about 7 years behind the Gregorian calendar.
FJI: Fiji consists of 332 islands, of which only 110 are inhabited. Its waters contain some of the most biodiverse coral reef systems on Earth.
FIN: Finland has more saunas than cars — an estimated 3.3 million saunas for a population of just 5.5 million people.
FRA: France is the most visited country in the world, attracting around 90 million tourists per year — more than its entire population.
GAB: Gabon has set aside 11% of its land as national parks — one of the highest percentages in the world — protecting its dense rainforests.
GMB: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa and is almost entirely surrounded by Senegal, running along the Gambia River.
GEO: Georgia is one of the world's oldest wine-producing regions, with evidence of winemaking dating back 8,000 years using clay vessels called qvevri.
DEU: Germany is the world's second-largest book market and has over 1,500 breweries, producing more than 5,000 varieties of beer.
GHA: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah's leadership.
GRC: Greece has the longest coastline in the Mediterranean Sea at 13,676 km, and about 80% of the country is covered by mountains.
GRD: Grenada is known as the "Isle of Spice" and is the world's second-largest producer of nutmeg after Indonesia.
GTM: Guatemala is home to Tikal, one of the largest archaeological sites of the ancient Maya civilisation, deep within tropical rainforest.
GIN: Guinea contains the Fouta Djallon highlands, the source of the Niger, Gambia, and Senegal rivers — often called "West Africa's water tower."
GNB: Guinea-Bissau's Bijagós Archipelago, made up of 88 islands, is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and one of West Africa's richest marine ecosystems.
GUY: Guyana is home to Kaieteur Falls, one of the world's most powerful waterfalls — roughly five times the height of Niagara Falls.
HTI: Haiti was the first Black republic in the world and the first Caribbean nation to gain independence, following a slave revolution in 1804.
HND: Honduras is home to the ancient Maya city of Copán, renowned for its intricately carved stone stelae and hieroglyphic stairway.
HUN: Hungary has the largest natural thermal lake in the world suitable for swimming — Lake Hévíz — which remains warm even in winter.
ISL: Iceland is the world's oldest parliamentary democracy, with the Althing parliament established in 930 AD and still in operation today.
IND: India is the world's largest democracy by population and is home to 4 of the world's 6 classical dance forms recognised by UNESCO.
IDN: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago nation, consisting of over 17,000 islands stretching across 5,100 km of ocean.
IRN: Iran (Persia) is home to one of the world's oldest civilisations and has the largest network of ancient underground water channels (qanats) on Earth.
IRQ: Iraq is home to Mesopotamia, often called "the Cradle of Civilisation," where writing, the wheel, and the first cities were invented.
IRL: Ireland ranks among the highest in the world for per capita tea consumption and is famous for a tea-drinking culture dating back centuries.
ISR: Israel has the highest number of scientists and technicians per capita in the world and more tech start-ups per capita than any other nation.
ITA: Italy is home to more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country — 58 sites as of 2024, including Rome, Venice, and Florence.
JAM: Jamaica is the birthplace of reggae music and the Rastafari religious movement, both of which have spread worldwide from this small island.
JPN: Japan has the world's oldest continuously operating company — Kongō Gumi, a construction firm founded in 578 AD, active for over 1,400 years.
JOR: Jordan is home to Petra, the ancient Nabataean city carved entirely into rose-red sandstone cliffs, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
KAZ: Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country, covering 2.7 million sq km — larger than Western Europe.
KEN: Kenya is home to the Maasai Mara, where the world's largest animal migration occurs annually, with over 1.5 million wildebeest crossing.
KIR: Kiribati spans 3 time zones and is among the first countries to welcome each new day. It faces an existential threat from rising sea levels.
PRK: North Korea operates on its own time zone, set 30 minutes behind South Korea — a change introduced in 2015 as a symbolic gesture of independence.
KOR: South Korea is the world's leading exporter of cultural content after the USA, driven by K-pop, K-drama, and Korean cinema globally.
UNK: Kosovo declared independence in 2008 and is one of the youngest countries in the world, recognised by over 100 UN member states.
KWT: Kuwait has the world's sixth-largest oil reserves and covers only 17,818 sq km — making it one of the wealthiest nations per capita.
KGZ: Kyrgyzstan is the only country whose flag features a representation of a traditional dwelling — the yurt's roof ring (tunduk) on its red flag.
LAO: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per capita in history — over 2 million tonnes of ordnance were dropped during the Vietnam War era.
LVA: Latvia has one of the world's fastest average internet speeds and is a global leader in information technology exports per capita.
LBN: Lebanon is home to the Cedars of God — some of the oldest trees on Earth, referenced in the Epic of Gilgamesh and the Bible.
LSO: Lesotho is the only country in the world entirely surrounded by another country — South Africa — and lies entirely above 1,000 metres elevation.
LBR: Liberia was founded in 1822 by formerly enslaved Americans and became Africa's first republic, with a constitution modelled on that of the USA.
LBY: Libya has the largest proven oil reserves in Africa, accounting for approximately 3% of the world's total known oil supply.
LIE: Liechtenstein is the world's largest producer of false teeth (dentures) and one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.
LTU: Lithuania was the last pagan country in Europe before converting to Christianity in 1387 — the final nation on the continent to do so.
LUX: Luxembourg has one of the highest GDP per capita figures in the world and is home to the European Court of Justice and other EU institutions.
MDG: Madagascar is one of the world's most biodiverse islands — about 90% of its wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.
MWI: Lake Malawi contains more species of fish than any other lake in the world — over 1,000 species, most of them cichlids.
MYS: Malaysia is home to the world's largest flower, the Rafflesia arnoldii, which can grow up to 1 metre in diameter.
MDV: The Maldives is the world's lowest-lying country, with an average ground level of just 1.5 metres above sea level, threatened by rising seas.
MLI: Mali is home to Djenné, whose Great Mosque is the world's largest mud-brick structure and is traditionally rebuilt by the community every year.
MLT: Malta is the smallest EU member state by both area and population, with a recorded human history stretching back over 7,000 years.
MHL: The Marshall Islands was the site of 67 nuclear tests conducted by the USA between 1946 and 1958, causing lasting environmental damage.
MRT: Mauritania is one of the few countries where slavery was only officially criminalised as recently as 2007, though it continues to persist in practice.
MUS: Mauritius was home to the dodo, a flightless bird that went extinct in the 17th century — its image remains a national symbol.
MEX: Mexico City is built on the site of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán and is one of the world's largest cities by population.
FSM: The Federated States of Micronesia spans nearly 3 million sq km of the Pacific Ocean but has a total land area of only 702 sq km.
MDA: Moldova is one of the world's top wine producers per capita and home to the Milestii Mici wine cellar — the world's largest wine collection.
MCO: Monaco is the world's most densely populated country and the second smallest by area, covering just 2.02 sq km in total.
MNG: Mongolia has the lowest population density of any country on Earth and is home to the world's largest contiguous grassland, the Eurasian Steppe.
MNE: Montenegro's name means "Black Mountain" in both Montenegrin and Italian — a reference to the dark appearance of Mount Lovćen.
MAR: Morocco is the only African country with coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
MOZ: Mozambique's flag is the only national flag in the world to feature a modern weapon — an AK-47 rifle — alongside a hoe and an open book.
MMR: Myanmar is home to the Irrawaddy dolphin, a critically endangered freshwater dolphin found only in select rivers in Southeast Asia.
NAM: Namibia's Namib Desert is the world's oldest desert, estimated to be 55–80 million years old, and gave the country its name.
NRU: Nauru is the world's smallest island nation and the third-smallest country overall, covering just 21 sq km in the Pacific Ocean.
NPL: Nepal is home to 8 of the world's 10 highest mountains, including Mount Everest — the highest point on Earth at 8,849 metres.
NLD: The Netherlands has more bicycles than people — about 23 million bikes for 17 million inhabitants — and 35,000 km of dedicated cycle paths.
NZL: New Zealand was the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote, in 1893, decades before most of the world.
NIC: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America and home to two of the region's largest freshwater lakes: Managua and Nicaragua.
NER: The Niger River, one of Africa's great rivers, flows through 9 countries and gives both Niger and Nigeria their names.
NGA: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country with over 220 million people and has the continent's largest economy by nominal GDP.
MKD: North Macedonia's capital Skopje was largely rebuilt after a devastating earthquake in 1963 that destroyed about 80% of the city.
NOR: Norway administers the Svalbard archipelago, home to more polar bears than people — about 3,000 bears versus a human population of around 2,600.
OMN: Oman is home to the ancient frankincense trade route, linked to Boswellia trees — the source of frankincense resin — recognised as a UNESCO site.
PAK: Pakistan is home to K2, the world's second-highest mountain at 8,611 metres, considered more technically challenging to climb than Everest.
PLW: Palau was the first country to ban reef-toxic sunscreen in 2020 to protect its coral reefs, considered among the world's healthiest.
PAN: Panama is the only place on Earth where you can watch the sun rise over the Pacific and set over the Atlantic from the same spot.
PNG: Papua New Guinea has the greatest linguistic diversity of any country — over 800 languages spoken among its 10 million people.
PRY: Paraguay is one of only two landlocked countries in South America and generates almost all of its electricity from the Itaipú hydroelectric dam.
PER: Peru is home to Machu Picchu, the 15th-century Inca citadel high in the Andes, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
PHL: The Philippines is an archipelago of 7,641 islands and is home to the Chocolate Hills — over 1,200 symmetrical mounds on Bohol island.
POL: Poland has produced more Nobel Prize winners per capita than most countries, including Marie Curie, who won the prize twice.
PRT: Portugal is the oldest nation-state in Europe, with borders largely unchanged since 1139 AD — over 880 years of territorial continuity.
QAT: Qatar has the highest GDP per capita in the Arab world and transformed from a pearl-fishing economy into a gas superpower within 50 years.
ROU: Romania is home to Turda Salt Mine, a 2,000-year-old mine converted into an underground theme park with a Ferris wheel and mini golf.
RUS: Russia is the world's largest country, spanning 11 time zones and covering about 11% of the world's total land area.
RWA: Rwanda has one of the highest proportions of women in parliament in the world, with women holding over 60% of legislative seats.
KNA: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere, covering just 261 sq km in the Caribbean.
LCA: Saint Lucia is the only country in the world named after a woman — Saint Lucy of Syracuse — a Christian martyr from Sicily.
VCT: Saint Vincent is home to La Soufrière, an active volcano that last erupted in 2021 and one of the Caribbean's most active volcanoes.
WSM: Samoa moved the international date line in 2011, skipping an entire day to better align its calendar with Australia and New Zealand.
SMR: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest republic, founded in 301 AD, and is entirely surrounded by Italy.
STP: São Tomé and Príncipe lies at the intersection of the equator and the prime meridian — the geographic point known as (0°N, 0°E).
SAU: Saudi Arabia is the world's largest country with no permanent rivers — all water comes from aquifers, rainfall, or desalination plants.
SEN: Senegal's Pink Lake (Lac Rose) turns pink due to salt-loving algae — so salty that workers can walk on its crust to harvest salt.
SRB: Serbia is the world's largest exporter of raspberries, producing around 95,000 tonnes per year — roughly 30% of global supply.
SYC: The Seychelles is home to the world's largest seed — the Coco de Mer palm nut — which can weigh up to 25 kg.
SLE: Sierra Leone's name means "Lion Mountains" in Portuguese, given by explorer Pedro de Sintra in 1462 for the thunder-like sounds heard on its coast.
SGP: Singapore is the world's only city-state island nation and has no natural freshwater sources — it imports water and recycles nearly all of it.
SVK: Slovakia has more castles and châteaux per capita than any other country in the world — over 180 surviving castle structures.
SVN: Slovenia is the first country in the world to declare beekeeping a protected cultural heritage and bees a national symbol.
SLB: The Solomon Islands was the site of intense WWII Pacific battles and still has unexploded ordnance and sunken warships visible in its waters.
SOL: Somaliland was briefly independent for five days in June 1960 before voluntarily joining Somalia; it restored its separate sovereignty claim in 1991.
SOM: Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa at 3,333 km and was historically known as the "Land of Punt" in ancient Egyptian records.
ZAF: South Africa is the only country in the world to have voluntarily dismantled its own nuclear weapons programme, doing so in the early 1990s.
SSD: South Sudan is the world's newest internationally recognised country, having gained independence from Sudan on 9 July 2011.
ESP: Spain has the world's second-largest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites and is home to Europe's oldest restaurant, Sobrino de Botín, open since 1725.
LKA: Sri Lanka is the world's leading exporter of Ceylon tea and has the highest biodiversity density of any Asian country relative to its size.
SDN: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt — over 200 Nubian pyramids built by the Kushite kingdoms stretch across its desert landscape.
SUR: Suriname is the most forested country in the world by percentage — over 93% of its land area is covered by tropical rainforest.
SWE: Sweden invented the three-point seatbelt, dynamite, the pacemaker, the refrigerator, and flat-pack furniture — all within 150 years.
CHE: Switzerland has over 1,500 lakes and is the source of major European rivers including the Rhine, Rhône, and Inn.
SYR: Syria is home to Damascus, widely considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, settled for over 11,000 years.
TJK: Tajikistan is the most mountainous country in Central Asia — over 93% of its territory consists of mountains above 1,000 metres.
TZA: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak at 5,895 metres, and the Serengeti, site of the great wildebeest migration.
THA: Thailand is the world's largest exporter of rice and is home to the world's largest gold Buddha statue, at Bangkok's Wat Traimit temple.
TLS: Timor-Leste (East Timor) became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century, gaining full independence on 20 May 2002.
TGO: Togo is home to the Grand Marché de Lomé, one of West Africa's largest and oldest markets, famously managed entirely by women traders.
TON: Tonga is the only monarchy in the Pacific and was never formally annexed as a colony — it signed a treaty of friendship with Britain in 1900.
TTO: Trinidad and Tobago is the birthplace of both the steelpan musical instrument and the Carnival tradition in the Caribbean.
TUN: Tunisia is home to the ancient city of Carthage, once Rome's greatest rival, and has Africa's northernmost point at Ras ben Sakka.
TUR: Turkey is home to Göbekli Tepe, the world's oldest known temple complex, built around 9600 BC — 6,000 years before Stonehenge.
TKM: Turkmenistan's Darvaza gas crater — the "Door to Hell" — has been burning continuously since Soviet engineers set it alight in 1971.
TUV: Tuvalu is the world's fourth-smallest country and among the most threatened by rising sea levels — most of its land sits just 1–2 metres above sea level.
UGA: Uganda is home to half of the world's remaining mountain gorilla population, found in Bwindi Impenetrable Forest National Park.
UKR: Ukraine is the largest country located entirely within Europe and has the continent's most fertile agricultural land — the "black soil" belt.
ARE: The UAE is home to the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building at 828 metres, and the world's largest indoor theme park, in Dubai.
GBR: The UK is home to the world's oldest underground railway — the London Underground, opened in 1863 and still in daily operation.
USA: The USA has the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and is home to more Nobel Prize laureates than any other country.
URY: Uruguay was the first country in Latin America to fully legalise marijuana (2013), same-sex marriage (2013), and abortion (2012).
UZB: Uzbekistan is home to Samarkand, one of the oldest cities in Central Asia and a key stop on the ancient Silk Road trade route.
VUT: Vanuatu consistently ranks as one of the world's happiest countries and is home to Yasur, one of Earth's most accessible active volcanoes.
VAT: Vatican City is the world's smallest country, covering just 0.44 sq km, and is home to the world's largest church, St. Peter's Basilica.
VEN: Venezuela is home to Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 metres — nearly 20 times taller than Niagara Falls.
VNM: Vietnam is the world's second-largest exporter of coffee and is home to Ha Long Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of 1,600 limestone islands.
YEM: Yemen is home to Socotra Island, often called the "Galápagos of the Indian Ocean," where 37% of plant species are found nowhere else on Earth.
ZMB: Zambia shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe — the world's largest waterfall by combined width and height, known locally as "The Smoke That Thunders."
ZWE: Zimbabwe was home to the ancient Great Zimbabwe stone city — a 12th–15th century kingdom that gave the country its name.
